input.quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 gives Customer (not IBM) a convenience right at one month's notice, and IBM has no convenience right (Section 3.3 is breach-only), so notice and mutuality meet the preferred position. However, the exit is conditioned on early termination charges of unspecified amount set in Attachment A/Service Option Attachments, with no cap and no refund of prepaid fees. An uncapped exit penalty fails the fallback, which permits an early-termination fee only up to three months' fees. Consistent with the redline guidance we replaced the open-ended penalty with the fallback three-month cap and added a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; we left the favourable one-month notice period untouched.

ops.oldText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
ops.newText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, provided that such charges will not in the aggregate exceed the charges payable for three (3) months of the terminated Services. IBM will refund to Customer any fees prepaid for the period after the effective date of termination on a pro-rata basis.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We capped early termination charges at three months' fees and added a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, since our playbook does not accept uncapped exit penalties on a convenience termination. The one month's notice period already works for us.
proposal.summary: Cap Section 3.4(b) early termination charges at three months' fees and require pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
